title: Trim host orchestration latency in prefill→decode via zero-copy buffers and CPU affinity scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: In production traces we observe 15-45ms of per-request host-side overhead during the transition from prefill to decode for short-to-medium sequence lengths. Root causes identified: conservative memory copy paths (host<->device staging buffers), frequent threadpool wakeups and context switches in the CPU orchestrator, and lack of kernel-selection hints that would allow device kernels to avoid additional host coordination. Goal: reduce host-side latency by 30-50% for typical conversational workloads without regressing throughput or increasing memory pressure. Approach: 1) introduce a zero-copy pinned buffer lane for common prefill/kv-cache handoff patterns (mmap + cudaHostRegister equivalent), 2) implement a small lock-free ring to pass buffer descriptors between prefill threads and the GPU submission thread to avoid mutex contention and thread wakeups, 3) add CPU affinity scheduling (dedicated lightweight poller threads pinned to host CPU cores colocated with the GPU PCIe NUMA node) to reduce cross-socket latency, 4) add explicit kernel-selection hints in the orchestrator so the device runtime picks precompiled attention kernels when sequence lengths and quantization profiles match, eliminating an extra handoff step. Constraints: must be compatible with Dedicated and Private modes (no privileged host changes required), fit within existing memory budgets, and remain safe for multi-tenant Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Mean host-side prefill->decode latency reduced >= 30% on representative bench (conv-16/32 seq mix)
End-to-end p50 latency regression <= 5% for high-throughput workloads
No increase in out-of-memory rates above 1% from baseline
New ring buffer path covered by unit tests and stress-tested with long-running loadtest
Design doc and perf dashboard links provided and reviewed by runtime team
updates: 2026-01-21: Spike completed comparing cudaHostAlloc vs. pinned-page mmap on Linux. mmap path reduced copy syscall overhead by ~0.6ms in microbench.

2026-01-27: Prototype lock-free descriptor ring implemented (single-producer single-consumer) and integrated into dev harness. Initial runs show 12-18% host overhead reduction for short seq workloads.
2026-02-02: Added CPU affinity scheduling prototype. Pinning poller thread to PCIe-local core reduces cross-socket latency variance (p95 down ~20%).
2026-02-07: Kernel-selection hints API sketched in design doc; landed small API change to pass sequence-length histogram to kernel selector (internals-only flag).
2026-02-12: Ran dedicated capacity QA suite on a 4-GPU node with multi-tenant sim; observed small memory pressure spike when enabling pinned zero-copy buffers—investigating fallback thresholds.

2026-02-15: Design review with infra and dedicated teams. Action items: add per-tenant pinned-buffer quota, expand unit tests for NUMA scenarios, and add a defensive fallback that reverts to staged copies when pinned allocation fails.
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2389 (WIP prototype for ring buffer and zero-copy path)
benchmarks: Baseline (conv-16/32 mix): mean host prefill->decode overhead = 28.4ms
Prototype (zero-copy + ring + affinity): mean overhead = 17.6ms (38% reduction)
Throughput (tokens/s) unchanged within ±3% under 8-GPU linear loadtest
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Patel): strong signal on customer-facing latency reductions; ask to include regression tests for cold-start pinned allocations
Design (Lena Ortiz): prefer a configurable fallback to avoid degenerate behavior on memory-constrained hosts
Security (Priya Narang): confirm mmap-based path does not change syscall surface for Private deployments; flagged for 10m review
